what_its_for: Dichlorphenamide is used to treat periodic paralysis, which is a condition where your muscles suddenly become very weak or unable to move. It helps reduce how often these episodes happen and how severe they are. There are two main types it treats: hyperkalemic periodic paralysis (too much potassium in your blood during attacks) and hypokalemic periodic paralysis (too little potassium in your blood during attacks).
how_to_take: Take dichlorphenamide by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep it working consistently. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablets unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay to do so.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 50 mg taken twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening). Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well it works for you and how you tolerate it. The maximum dose is typically 200 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store dichlorphenamide at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place, such as a dresser drawer or cabinet — not in the bathroom, where it can be humid. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking dichlorphenamide, as it can increase the risk of side effects such as dizziness and confusion. Avoid activities that require mental alertness, such as driving or operating heavy machinery, until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause dizziness or confusion. Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Be careful in hot weather or during heavy exercise, as this medicine may make it harder for your body to cool itself (reduced sweating). Talk to your doctor before taking aspirin or other salicylate-containing products, as combining them with dichlorphenamide can be harmful.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe confusion or trouble thinking clearly, kidney stones (severe back or side pain, pain when urinating, blood in urine), signs of low potassium such as muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat, signs of low sodium such as headache, nausea, seizures, or feeling very confused, high blood ammonia levels (extreme tiredness, vomiting, unusual behavior, or loss of consciousness), eye pain or sudden changes in your vision, signs of severe allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, or any unusual or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Some patients notice fewer or less severe episodes of muscle weakness within the first few weeks of starting the medication. However, it may take several weeks of consistent use before you see the full benefit. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you feel well, because it works best when taken regularly to prevent episodes from happening.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over) may be more sensitive to side effects such as confusion and dizziness and should be monitored closely. This medication is not approved for use in children under 18 years old, so talk to your doctor if your child has periodic paralysis. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine, as the safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully established. People with kidney or liver problems may need dose adjustments or closer monitoring. Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting dichlorphenamide.
